title: Power Prices Triple on PJM as Heat Wave and Data Centers Collide

facts.claim: PJM Interconnection electricity demand surged to roughly 163 gigawatts on Thursday, nearly reaching the 2006 all-time peak of 165,563 megawatts.
facts.subject: PJM Interconnection
facts.cause: heat dome with heat indices past 110 degrees pushing peak demand

facts.claim: Day-ahead power prices topped $2,000 per megawatt-hour in parts of the PJM system on Thursday.
facts.subject: PJM electricity
facts.cause: brutal heat wave and data center demand surge

facts.claim: Western Hub power benchmark settled at $1,222.75/MWh, nearly triple where it stood during a comparable peak last summer.
facts.subject: Western Hub electricity
facts.cause: heat wave and record demand

facts.claim: PJM operating reserves sank to 5,091 MW on Thursday from 10,996 MW a day earlier.
facts.subject: PJM reserves
facts.cause: record demand from heat wave and data centers

facts.claim: PJM projects peak demand will grow by 32 gigawatts between 2024 and 2030, with all but 2 gigawatts of that increase coming from data centers.
facts.subject: PJM demand
facts.magnitude: 32 GW total, 30 GW from data centers
facts.cause: data center capacity expansion in region

facts.claim: PJM capacity market reached record $333.44 per megawatt-day, up more than 11-fold from $28.92 just three auctions earlier.
facts.subject: PJM capacity market
facts.cause: data center demand surge

facts.claim: US Department of Energy issued third emergency order of 2026, authorizing PJM to push power plants past normal pollution limits and force large data centers onto backup generators during peak hours.
facts.subject: PJM power grid
facts.cause: electricity demand surge pushing grid to edge of all-time records

title: OPEC Oil Production Jumps, But Gulf Supply Is Still Far From Normal

facts.claim: OPEC 11 members produced 19.43 million barrels per day in June, up 3.3 million bpd from May's lowest level recorded by Reuters survey since at least 2000.
facts.subject: OPEC crude oil production
facts.cause: Kuwait and Iran bringing shut-in barrels back online after Strait of Hormuz crisis disruptions

facts.claim: Iran restored crude oil production after the United States lifted its naval blockade of Iranian ports under a 60-day agreement.
facts.subject: Iran crude oil production
facts.cause: US naval blockade lift under 60-day agreement

facts.claim: Saudi Arabia and Iraq boosted crude output in June.
facts.subject: Saudi Arabia and Iraq crude production
facts.cause: gradually restarting wells that had been shut due to storage capacity and Hormuz traffic constraints

facts.claim: Tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains well below pre-war levels.
facts.subject: Hormuz tanker traffic
facts.cause: insurers and shipowners remaining cautious after repeated attacks on commercial vessels

facts.claim: United States posted record crude production of nearly 14 million barrels per day.
facts.subject: US crude oil production

facts.claim: UAE, now outside OPEC, is exporting record volumes of crude oil as it empties storage built up during the conflict.
facts.subject: UAE crude oil exports
facts.cause: drawdown of storage accumulated during Middle East conflict

facts.claim: Record crude production from the United States and UAE record exports are fueling renewed talk of oversupply and keeping pressure on crude prices.
facts.subject: crude oil prices
facts.cause: US and UAE record production and exports increasing supply

title: Japan services activity rebounds as input costs hit four-year inflation high

facts.claim: Japan services PMI Business Activity Index rose to 52.2 in June from 50.0 in May, signaling renewed growth.
facts.subject: Japan services sector
facts.cause: strong new work growth, particularly from domestic demand

facts.claim: Total new work in Japan services increased at one of the quickest rates in two years.
facts.subject: Japan services new business
facts.cause: firmer domestic demand from upcoming events and greater business activity

facts.claim: Japan services input prices rose at their fastest pace since June 2022, a four-year high.
facts.subject: Japan input cost inflation
facts.cause: increases in oil, energy, food and wage costs, compounded by Middle East war supply chain pressure

facts.claim: Japan services output prices rose at a further strong increase, though easing slightly from May's near-record high.
facts.subject: Japan services output prices
facts.cause: pass-through of elevated input costs to customers

facts.claim: Japan services new export orders rose at their slowest pace in six months as overseas demand for Japanese services fell markedly amid lower tourist numbers.
facts.subject: Japan export demand
facts.cause: lower inbound tourist numbers and subdued overseas demand

facts.claim: Japan services employment growth was mild in June, with firms increasing staff at a quicker pace than May but below the past year's average.
facts.subject: Japan services employment
facts.cause: modest business expansion despite cost pressures

facts.claim: Japan services business confidence in the year-ahead outlook remained subdued, among the lowest levels since the pandemic.
facts.subject: Japan business confidence
facts.cause: Middle East war uncertainty, rising costs, and labour shortages

facts.claim: Japan Composite Output Index rose to 52.8 in June from 51.1 in May, the quickest pace of growth in three months.
facts.subject: Japan private sector output
facts.cause: combined growth in both manufacturing and services sectors
